claims.text: Cyclic mechanical loading at 300–500°C induces localized nanoscale compositional fluctuations in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy.
The stress-induced compositional fluctuations trigger intragranular chemically ordered regions.
The intragranular ordered regions behave as brittle microstructural precipitates.
The ordered regions concentrate strain and nucleate cracks.
Crack nucleation at the ordered regions causes brittle behavior despite a predominantly homogeneous, disordered matrix.
The proposed initial material is a homogeneous, disordered, single-phase compositionally complex high-entropy alloy.
Cyclic loading at intermediate temperature provokes stress-assisted atomic diffusion.
The ordered regions form through local segregation of minor alloying elements.
Mechanical strain promotes short-range atomic diffusion that overcomes local energy barriers.
Strain-assisted diffusion clusters selected elements into ordered intragranular arrangements.
Conventional-alloy brittle behavior is linked primarily to grain-boundary segregation or intergranular precipitation.
TEM or atom-probe tomography will reveal nanoscale ordered intragranular regions after cyclic loading.
Fracture analysis will locate crack initiation at the nanoscale ordered regions.
Monotonically loaded specimens at comparable temperatures will lack the ordered regions.
Monotonically loaded specimens at comparable temperatures will retain ductile behavior.
The proposed embrittlement occurs around 300–500°C at cyclic stress amplitudes near the alloy's yield strength.
Ordered-region formation and associated brittle behavior are not expected under purely monotonic loading or at temperatures far outside 300–500°C.
Identical cyclically and monotonically loaded specimens tested at the same temperature provide the proposed controlled comparison.
Absence of nanoscale intragranular ordering after cyclic loading would falsify the hypothesis.
Observation of brittle fracture governed by conventional grain-boundary precipitation rather than intragranular features would falsify the hypothesis.
